claims: Nuclear chirality energy splitting stems from both inter-well tunneling and non-orthogonal overlap <L|R> != 0; splitting persists even when tunneling vanishes.

Experimental energy differences Delta E(I) in 9 representative odd-odd chiral candidates do not follow the naive 'rapid decrease and high-spin stabilization' rule, showing near-constant splitting or moment-of-inertia divergence.

B(M1) staggering is governed by S-symmetry; the asymmetry in 128Cs below 15 hbar (vanishing in yrast band, amplified in partner band) proves S-symmetry holds while chirality dissolves into planar geometry.
Plunger RDDS lifetimes in 128Cs confirm that the 10+ state lifetime is 9 +- 5 ps, ruling out staggering extrapolation and confirming staggering collapses before 10+.

The g-factor of the 56 ns isomeric 9+ bandhead in 128Cs directly measures the volume spanned by the three spins and proves a near-planar non-chiral geometry, establishing a non-chiral to chiral transition between 9 hbar and 14 hbar.

boundary: 2x2 mixing is a discrete truncation that does not model continuous aplanarity wavefunctions
